page.layout: One page: at the head, the printed page number; below it a woodcut ornamental border; then the centred title block in roman, italic and capitals, ending with THEOREMATA.; One column of numbered paragraphs (1–10) at left, with marginal notes in italic type down the right margin; below the text, a centred gathering mark "a".

main_text.p: 1 Ars liberalis est doctrina, qua hominem verè literatum Definitur ars liberalis in genere. & doctum reddit.
3 Dividitur ars liberalis in genere.Ars externa est systema methodicum certorum praeceptorum de re aliqua scibilis utilisque traditorum, ad erudiendum & perficiendum hominem.
4 In ea consideranda veniunt, partim natura, partim differentia. Ars externa quid sit.
5 Natura artis liberalis externae cognoscitur partim ex causis, partim ex legibus. Causa artis externa exponuntur.
6 Causa sunt partim finis & efficiens: partim Materia & Forma.
7 Finis est vel ultimus, vel subordinatus.
8 I. Finis.Ultimus finis vel est simpliciter ultimus, vel secundum quid ultimus.
9 Simpliciter finis ultimus, est gloria Dei per artes illustranda.
10 Secundum quid ultimus, est perfectio certa hominis, quam ars sibi propositam habet, ad succurrendum humana indigentia & necessitati.

page.notes: The woodcut border above the title is an ornament with no text and is not transcribed. "seu" is set in italic script. The title lines are transcribed as printed, with the printed hyphens kept at the two line ends. Doubtful: the accent on "verè" in paragraph 1 may be a printed grave mark rather than an accent; copied as seen. The margin notes are set in italic and are copied as such.
